headline: Recommended that the Town Council use conservation funds to buy 144 Rear Wildwood Road, which would protect Black Brook.
summary: Members raised concerns about one exit and condo management for the Pillsbury Road plan, and about a stormwater buffer impact at 7 Litchfield Road. Old business covered trail work, a rabbit habitat meeting, and an unlocked Eversource gate.
decisions: Recommended unanimously that the Town Council purchase Map 3 Lot 9, 144 Rear Wildwood Road.

decision_evidence.quote: M. Speltz moved to recommend that the Town Council purchase Map 3 Lot 9 as outlined in the slides. D. Heafey seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.

plain_text:
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, September 8, 2026
Draft Minutes
1 Present: Marge Badois, Chair; Deb Lievens, member; Bob Maxwell, member; David Heafey, member; 
2 Elkel Bickford, member; Michael Speltz, alternate member; Gary Della Grotta, alternate member; Susan 
3 Malouin, alternate member
4
5 Absent: Gene Harrington, Vice Chair
6
7 Also present: Michael Bazegian, GIS Manager/Comprehensive Planner
8
9
10 Call to Order and Roll Call
11 Ms. Badois called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m. She appointed Michael Speltz to vote for Gene 
12 Harrington and Gary Della Grotta for the vacant position. 
13
14 DRC – 44 & 36 Pillsbury Road - Subdivision/LLA - Map 10 Lot 15 & 42
15 The applicant was not present. A letter was received from Laura Gandia, attorney with Devine, Millimet 
16 & Branch, describing the proposal. 
17
18 This is a proposed subdivision and condominium conversion. The Commission discussed that the original 
19 plan was to construct 310 dwelling units, 250 of which would be rental cottages. The current plan is to 
20 turn some of the rental cottages into condominiums for sale, for a total of 151 condos. The Commission 
21 expressed concern about there being only one exit and it being located near the new traffic light at 
22 Michaels Way. 
23
24 The Commission expressed concern about accountability, as it will be difficult for a condo association to 
25 manage such a large number of condominiums. They discussed requiring a professional management 
26 company as opposed to a homeowners association. They noted that this plan will reduce the possibility 
27 for families to obtain affordable housing. Although this is not a conservation issue, it does address 
28 concerns about a condo association enforcing rules that do affect conservation values.
29
30 The Commission questioned whether the developer would have to observe the conservation overlay 
31 district, in spite of being grandfathered, as this constitutes a subdivision.
32
33 The Commission noted the short timeframe to submit their comments to the Planning Board, as they will
34 be hearing this case the next day.
35
36 M. Speltz noted he was an abutter, so asked that his comments be considered as those of a resident.
37
38 Commission Comments: Will the developer have to observe the conservation overlay district, as this 
39 constitutes a subdivision. A professional management company should be required, as opposed to a 
40 homeowners association. When the Planning Board approved the plan for 250 cottages, did they rely on

41 any statements, implied or given, that the approval would increase the amount of affordable housing in 
42 Londonderry. 
43
44 DRC – 7 Litchfield Road - Subdivision - Map 12 Lot 20
45 The applicant was not present.
46
47 The Commission noted that they requested that the water line cross the narrowest part of the wetlands. 
48 The plan shows that this has been done. They also requested that the entrance be moved. 
49
50 There is a significant buffer encroachment to accommodate the stormwater basin. The Commission 
51 reviewed their comments from the January 14, 2025 meeting, where they addressed the encroachment. 
52
53 The Commission noted the developer created the need to run a sewer line across the wetlands by 
54 cutting off and selling the lot on the northwest corner. The Commission now has to make concessions to 
55 accommodate the sewer line. 
56
57 The Commission noted the existence of a buffer impact policy that requires mitigation, but does not 
58 state what the mitigation is; the Commission provides a list of suggestions specific to the location. They 
59 noted the developer transferred a strip of land to the Town for the cemetery.
60
61 Commission Comments: Attempts should be made to preserve the maple tree near the entrance. The 
62 Commission remains concerned about the unduly large impact to the buffer to Little Cohas Brook by the 
63 stormwater structure in the northeast corner. If there is no other engineering solution, consider 
64 eliminating the first unit. 
65
66 Public Hearing - Acquisition of 144 Rear Wildwood Road
67 M. Speltz presented a proposal to acquire land at Map 3 Lot 9, just off Mammoth Road. He described the
68 parcel as primarily wetlands and densely vegetated. The parcel is identified by the surveyed lots on 
69 either side. While the deed lists the property as being 1.5 acres, M. Speltz felt it was larger, and asked M.
70 Bazegian to research this.
71
72 He explained this purchase would protect Black Brook and continue a long set of protections along the 
73 brook. 
74
75 The assessed value of the property is $23,300. The property owner is willing to accept this amount, less 
76 any transaction costs. 
77
78 There were no members of the public present to offer comment. M. Badois reported receipt of a 
79 comment from a resident asking why they would pay for land that cannot be built on because it is worth
80 nothing.
81
Londonderry Conservation Commission
Tuesday, September 8, 2026
Draft Minutes
82 The Commission agreed to recommend to the Town Council that conservation funds be used to 
83 purchase this property. 
84
85 M. Speltz moved to recommend that the Town Council purchase Map 3 Lot 9 as outlined in the slides. 
86 D. Heafey seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.
87
88 Public Comment
89 There were no members of the public present.
90
91 Old Business
92
93 Trail Work
94 M. Badois reported that Josh Cook with Trailways is planning a workday on the Mathes Trail. B. Maxwell 
95 has done some work to open the trail. The Commission discussed whether it was not being used because
96 it was overgrown, or vice versa. M. Speltz said NHF&G would need to be notified, once the date is 
97 scheduled.
98
99 Rabbit Habitat
100 Ms. Badois is meeting with someone at NHF&G on September 10th via Zoom to discuss rabbit habitat.
101
102 Unlocked Eversource Gate
103 M. Badois reported there is an Eversource gate on Litchfield Road at the Cooper parcel that is not locked.
104 She believes trucks are entering the gate and crossing the brook. She will research who should be 
105 contacted at Eversource to lock the gate. 
106
107 Hickory Hill
108 B. Maxwell reported he has cleared the access to the Hickory Hill kiosk from the old and new parking 
109 lots. M. Badois will contact DPW about the trail being cleared.
110
111 Lithia Spring
112 M. Speltz has tried to contact the old owner of Penny Fence Company to discuss parking at Lithia Spring, 
113 but has not been successful. Another solution is needed.
114
115 Trail Grants
116 M. Speltz noted trail grants were supposed to be announced in August, but he has not heard anything.
117
118 Financial Report
119 D. Lievens offered a financial update through June 30th. 
120
121 New Business
